investors.name: Brad Gerstner

philosophy.title: Market leadership and durable economics
philosophy.text: Altimeter describes research into future market leaders, addressable markets, management teams, competitive moats, unit economics and reasonable valuation.

philosophy.title: Research across public and private markets
philosophy.text: The firm describes fundamental, bottom-up work and a long time horizon spanning public and private technology businesses.

philosophy.title: Capital discipline and shareholder returns
philosophy.text: His 2022 Meta letter challenged excessive operating expenditure and requested greater discipline around large growth investments.

research_questions: Can the company dominate a large market while sustaining attractive unit economics?
Does management convert growth spending into operating cash and durable competitive advantage?
Are downstream customers economically capable of paying for AI infrastructure?
At today's valuation, what must go right and what would invalidate the thesis?
investors.manager_process_note: Questions above are a DEDL research interpretation, NOT Altimeter's unpublished rules or a mechanical DEDL score.

investors.name: Li Lu
investors.focus: Business ownership, economic moats and disciplined valuation

philosophy.title: Businesses, not ticker symbols
philosophy.text: Himalaya describes long-term ownership of high-quality businesses with significant moats, growth potential and trustworthy management.

philosophy.title: Patience and concentration
philosophy.text: The firm publishes Li Lu's fat-pitch analogy: most opportunities can be passed over; act decisively when an unusually strong opportunity appears.

philosophy.title: Margin of safety and limits of knowledge
philosophy.text: Li Lu's Columbia discussion emphasizes understanding a business, knowing what one does not know, and requiring a margin of safety.

research_questions: Could we explain this business as if we owned all of it?
Is its economic moat observable in cash flows and competitive behavior?
What does management do when circumstances become adverse?
Is the valuation sufficiently conservative given what is uncertain?
investors.manager_process_note: Questions above are a DEDL research interpretation, NOT Himalaya's unpublished rules or a mechanical DEDL score.

investors.name: Chris Hohn
investors.focus: Concentrated long-term ownership, business quality, activism and capital allocation

philosophy.title: Focused ownership and engagement
philosophy.basis: Publicly observed activist governance practice; research interpretation
philosophy.text: Study whether shareholder engagement, operating discipline and improved capital allocation can improve returns. This is an analytical lens, not TCI's complete internal process.

philosophy.title: Durable cash-producing franchises
philosophy.basis: Inferred from reported holdings; not a manager statement
philosophy.text: Reported holdings emphasize payments, ratings, transportation networks and installed-base industrial services. We will test moat durability rather than assume it from portfolio membership.

philosophy.title: Concentration also raises drawdown risk
philosophy.text: A strong franchise can still be a poor purchase if expectations are too high or activism fails. Compare engagements against non-engaged peers and discontinued investments.

research_questions: Can recurring cash flow and capital allocation explain returns independent of sector and size?
Does public engagement precede measurable ROIC, governance or cash-flow improvements?
What happens when the holding is expensive, when the activist thesis fails, or when the position is exited?
Would a matched quality-business control portfolio do just as well without activism?
investors.manager_process_note: REDL experimental questions; NOT TCI's unpublished rules. Only public filing facts are attributed to TCI.

investors.name: Dev Kantesaria
investors.focus: Concentrated compounding businesses, recurring economics and barriers to entry

philosophy.title: Pricing power and limited competition
philosophy.text: Ratings, decision scores, payments and lithography suggest an emphasis on businesses with difficult-to-replicate advantages; this is a hypothesis, not a verified quote.

philosophy.title: Quality of compounding
philosophy.basis: REDL hypothesis; not a published numerical rule
philosophy.text: Test whether reinvestment returns, recurring revenue, retention, pricing power and incremental margins predict future free cash flow without paying excessive valuation multiples.

philosophy.title: Avoid mistaking business quality for entry quality
philosophy.text: Even very strong moats can disappoint if valuations compress. Compare price paid, cash yield and returns from high-quality stocks versus quality-neutral matched peers.

research_questions: Can high ROIC and recurring cash flow forecast multi-year business results after valuation controls?
Are rating and network businesses resilient across recession, regulation and interest-rate regimes?
When is an exceptional business too expensive to buy?
Do actual exits and reductions show when the hypothesis no longer applies?
investors.manager_process_note: REDL experimental questions inferred from publicly disclosed holdings; NOT a claim about Valley Forge's internal screens.

redl.name: Redesigning Equity Decision Loop
redl.principle: Study documented processes, propose falsifiable candidate rules, test against contemporaneous non-holdings and exited positions, and permit only independently validated, approved revisions to a future DEDL version. Do not retrofit daily DEDL judgments.

bias_controls.title: Survivorship and selection
bias_controls.control: Add failed funds, former star managers, fund closures and matched non-held candidate stocks; keep delisted tickers.

bias_controls.title: Disclosure and hindsight
bias_controls.failure: Treating a June 30 filing as known on June 30
bias_controls.control: Use SEC acceptance timestamp as earliest knowable holdings; wait for filing publication in simulated strategies.

bias_controls.title: Unobserved trades and assets
bias_controls.failure: Assuming U.S. 13F equals complete portfolio and every change is a discretionary trade
bias_controls.control: Mark 13F partial coverage, corporate actions, options and shares adjusted for splits; no inferred execution prices.

bias_controls.title: Market regime and factor mimicry
bias_controls.failure: Misreading simple quality/momentum/sector effects as manager-specific alpha
bias_controls.control: Matched industry, size, quality, valuation and momentum controls across inflation, credit and growth regimes.

bias_controls.title: Overfitting
bias_controls.failure: Searching thousands of thresholds until historical winners fit
bias_controls.control: Register hypotheses and falsification criteria first; hold out subsequent time periods, log rejected experiments.

bias_controls.title: Realistic replication
bias_controls.failure: Backtesting without commissions, taxes, spreads or turnover
bias_controls.control: Model delayed signals, feasible liquidity, SG investor taxes/FX and transaction costs; compare buy-and-hold and benchmarks.
